questions.explanation: One-syllable adjectives add '-er' for comparative
'Less' is used to compare to a lower degree

questions.sentence: This is ___ book I've ever read.
questions.explanation: Superlatives always use 'the': 'the best', 'the tallest'

questions.sentence: This test is ___ than the last one.
questions.grammar_rule: Comparative of long adjectives: more + adjective
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Uzun sifatlar qiyosiy darajasi: more + sifat
questions.explanation: Long adjectives (3+ syllables) use 'more' + adjective

questions.sentence: She runs as ___ as her brother.
questions.explanation: 'As...as' uses the base form of the adjective

questions.sentence: He is more taller than his father.
questions.correct_answer: He is taller than his father.
questions.explanation: Don't double compare: either 'taller' OR 'more tall', not both

questions.sentence: The situation is getting worse and ___.
questions.explanation: 'Worse and worse' = continuously getting more bad

questions.grammar_rule: 'The + comparative, the + comparative' for parallel changes
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'The + qiyosiy, the + qiyosiy' parallel o'zgarishlar uchun
questions.explanation: 'The more X, the more Y' shows proportional relationship

questions.correct_answer: Mary is not as tall as John.
questions.explanation: 'A is taller than B' = 'B is not as tall as A'

questions.sentence: This is by far ___ restaurant in town.
questions.explanation: 'By far' is used to emphasize a superlative = definitely the best

questions.sentence: She is the most prettiest girl in class.
questions.correct_answer: She is the prettiest girl in class.
questions.grammar_rule: Don't double superlatives: either -est OR most, not both
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Ikki ustunlik darajasi ishlatilmaydi: -est YOKI most
questions.explanation: Use 'prettiest' or 'most pretty' (informal), but never both together

questions.sentence: The problem is ___ than we thought.
questions.explanation: 'Far/much/a lot + comparative' = significantly more

questions.original_sentence: If you practice more, you will get better.
questions.correct_answer: The more you practice, the better you will get.
questions.grammar_rule: 'The more..., the more...' shows proportional relationship
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'The more..., the more...' proporsional munosabatni ko'rsatadi
questions.explanation: Transform 'if...more' to 'the more...the more' structure
'Second to none' is an idiom meaning 'the best'

questions.sentence: He is ___ intelligent than his brother.
questions.explanation: 'No less than' means 'equally' or 'just as much as'

questions.sentence: She is elder than me by two years.
questions.correct_answer: She is older than me by two years.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Elder' = only for family members (elder brother); 'older' = general comparison
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Elder' = faqat oila a'zolari uchun; 'older' = umumiy taqqoslash
questions.explanation: 'Elder' is only used as an adjective before nouns (my elder brother), not with 'than'

questions.sentence: The weather today is ___ better than yesterday.
questions.grammar_rule: Use 'slightly/a bit/a little' for small differences in comparatives
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Kichik farq uchun 'slightly/a bit/a little' ishlatiladi
questions.explanation: 'Slightly better' = a little better (small improvement)

questions.original_sentence: Nothing is more important than health.
questions.correct_answer: Health is the most important thing.
hints: 'Nothing is more X than Y' = 'Y is the most X'
questions.grammar_rule: 'Nothing is more X than Y' = 'Y is the most X'
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Nothing is more X than Y' = 'Y is the most X'
questions.explanation: Transform double negative comparison to superlative

questions.grammar_rule: 'The less/fewer..., the better' for negative comparisons
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Salbiy taqqoslash uchun 'The less/fewer..., the better'
questions.explanation: 'Less' for uncountable (talk = uncountable in 'less said')

questions.sentence: This car is ___ superior to that one.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives (superior, inferior) use 'to', not 'than', and no 'more'
